clue.text: Asian taking in air from island

indicators.note: the Asian word swallows the word for air, which goes inside it

parts.note: a Malay is a native of Malaysia or the Malay peninsula
gas is a loose synonym for air, both being vapour you cannot see

explanation.surface: An Asian traveller from an island breathes in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: Malagasy is both the people and the language of Madagascar, the large island off south-east Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes anything native to Madagascar, an island nation in the Indian Ocean.

clue.text: Came across old photo of the forehead

parts.note: to come across someone is to meet them; the past tense is met
a pic is a casual word for a photograph

explanation.surface: Someone stumbled upon an old snapshot showing a person's brow.
explanation.definitionFit: An anatomical adjective for the frontal bone, as in the metopic suture running down the brow.

clue.text: Story — name missing from plot

indicators.note: the letter for name is absent from the word for plot

parts.note: the plot of a play or novel is its story line, or simply line

explanation.surface: A tale with a character's name left out of the plot.
explanation.definitionFit: A story can mean a falsehood, as when a child is told not to tell stories.

clue.text: Fruit in a commercial being eaten by ape — nothing left

indicators.note: the commercial phrase goes inside the ape, as food goes into a mouth
nothing is left of the circle in the ape's name: it is removed

parts.note: the gorilla is the largest of the apes
O, the round zero, stands for nothing
the article a has the form an before a vowel
an ad is a television or radio commercial

explanation.surface: A fruit in an advert is gobbled up by an ape until nothing is left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nothing left' does two jobs in turn: 'nothing' is the round letter, and 'left' says it departs from the ape. 'in' just links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The passion fruit and its relatives are known by this Spanish-derived name.

clue.text: Sour companion's way, having little to hide?

indicators.note: the street abbreviation has the small word tucked away inside it

parts.note: ST, short for street, is a common crossword way
wee is Scottish and informal English for small

explanation.surface: A grumpy friend's path, with little to conceal.
explanation.walkthrough: In Chinese cookery, sour's partner is sweet, as in sweet and sour; the 's stands for is. 'having' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: The pairing sweet and sour makes each word the natural partner of the other.

clue.text: Defence is needed by a club

indicators.note: the word is follows and is wanted by the words a club

parts.note: a bat is a club used in cricket or baseball

explanation.surface: A defence needs a club to back it up.
explanation.definitionFit: An abatis is a barricade of felled trees with sharpened branches facing an attacker.

clue.text: Public transport variable and crowded

parts.note: a bus is a public transport vehicle
in algebra x, y and z are variables, so Y can stand for one

explanation.surface: Public transport is unpredictable and packed.
explanation.definitionFit: A busy place is full of people and activity.

clue.text: Hard worker on heroin's admitted losing the war

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on another sits below it, so the drug comes second

parts.note: to work like a Trojan is to work very hard
horse is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A diligent employee hooked on heroin confesses he has lost the battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitted' looks like a confession; it is the wooden horse being let into Troy, which cost the Trojans the war. The 's stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greeks hid soldiers inside a wooden horse; once the Trojans brought it within their walls, the city fell.

clue.text: Look deeper, said queen Jane

indicators.note: the phrase for looking deeper is spoken, giving the sound of a surname

parts.note: to look deeper is to see more

explanation.surface: Someone urges a deeper look, according to a queen called Jane.
explanation.walkthrough: Jane Seymour was the third wife of Henry VIII of England and mother of Edward VI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudor queen consort who married Henry VIII in 1536 bore this family name.

clue.text: To flow at length: it's like some football matches

parts.note: to flood is to flow over in great volume
the word it, with its 's serving as is

explanation.surface: Water pours out at length, as at some football games.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening matches are played under powerful lights mounted on tall pylons round the pitch.

clue.text: What toddlers love at bedtime — nothing improving

explanation.surface: Small children want the familiar bedtime tale, though nothing gets any better.
explanation.definitionFit: Small children ask for a favourite tale read again and again; the idiom also means a situation that never changes.

clue.text: Such a gun devastating upon impact

indicators.note: something devastating wrecks things, so these words are broken and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A gun that causes devastation when it hits.
explanation.definitionFit: A shotgun or rifle reloaded by sliding the fore-end back and forth is named for that mechanism.

clue.text: Object to bagpipe-playing? Unbelievable!

parts.note: to mind something is to object to it
a piper fills the bag by blowing into it

explanation.surface: Someone who dislikes the sound of the pipes exclaims in disbelief.
explanation.definitionFit: Something astonishing enough to overwhelm the mind is called this, as an exclamation of wonder.

clue.text: Address pet about snack

indicators.note: the pieces are turned round, read from the end back to the start

parts.note: O is the vocative of address, as in O Lord
a cat is a typical household pet

explanation.surface: Someone speaks to their pet about a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns OCAT round. 'Address' looks like a verb, but it is the poetic O used when calling out to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mexican folded tortilla filled with meat or beans is a common quick bite.

clue.text: Crane moving altar around church

indicators.note: the word for altar goes round the shuffled bird

parts.note: the Communion table is the altar in many churches

indicators.note: the bird's letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A crane is used to move an altar round a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' shuffles the bird into ERNAC; 'around' then wraps the altar word about it. The crane is not lifting anything: 'church' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabernacle is a place of worship, especially a nonconformist chapel or meeting house.

clue.text: Bishop may study hard

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart
firm means solid or hard

explanation.surface: A bishop might be studying hard.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is what a bishop does: in confirmation, a bishop lays hands on candidates to admit them fully to the church.
explanation.definitionFit: In Anglican and Catholic churches it is a bishop who administers the rite of confirmation.

clue.text: Twelve taking power, keeping identity and name secret

indicators.note: the word for power holds the other pieces safely inside it, keeping them secret

parts.note: might means strength or power
ID is short for identity

explanation.surface: Twelve people seize power while hiding who they are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping ... secret' together say the inner pieces are hidden away inside the word for power, just after its first letter. 'taking' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve o'clock at night is the hour that marks the turn of the day.

clue.text: Kid wanted meadow — almost got it

parts.note: a lea is a poetic word for a meadow or pasture

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: there! is what you say when you have got something right, and being there means understanding

explanation.surface: A child longed for a field and nearly managed it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child; it is the soft leather made from young goatskin. 'wanted' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Kid is fine soft material made from goatskin, used for gloves and shoes.

clue.text: Ferret appeared injured and moved awkwardly

parts.note: a hob is a male ferret
someone who bled showed signs of a wound

explanation.surface: A ferret looked hurt and limped about.
explanation.definitionFit: To hobble is to walk unsteadily or with a limp.

clue.text: Prince's outburst, admitting wife to be a fool

parts.note: Prince Hal is Shakespeare's name for the young Henry V

indicators.note: the outburst lets the wife in, so she goes inside it

parts.note: a fit is a sudden outburst of temper or emotion

explanation.surface: A prince's rage includes calling his wife an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Hal is the future Henry V in Shakespeare's Henry IV plays. 'to be' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A halfwit is a stupid person, with only half the usual intelligence.

clue.text: Article takes extra minute to shift, it's proved

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: the minute letter is shifted from the front to the end of the word for extra

parts.note: more means additional or extra

explanation.surface: An article needs one more minute to move, as is demonstrated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to shift' moves the M of MORE to its end, giving OREM. 'takes' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorem is a mathematical statement established by logical proof.

clue.text: Painter is beginning to slip, grabbed by ship's officer

indicators.note: the officer seizes the other pieces and holds them inside

parts.note: a mate is a deck officer on a merchant ship

indicators.note: the beginning of slip is its first letter

explanation.surface: A painter starting to slip is caught by a ship's officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was a French artist famed for bold colour and paper cut-outs.

clue.text: Cut out of circle — not informed one's out of it

definitions.text: Cut out of circle — not informed one's out of it

parts.words: Cut out of circle — not informed one's out of it
parts.note: the circle is also an inner group; someone excluded from it is uninformed, out of it in the idiom

explanation.surface: Someone left out of the group, unaware, is out of touch.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a ring shape, and the idioms in it and out of it mean informed and ignorant.

clue.text: Unhappiness with new wine at party

indicators.note: the new wine is placed at, following, the party

parts.note: a disco is a dance party
tent is a deep red Spanish wine used for communion

explanation.surface: Misery comes with fresh wine served at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: TENT is an old name for a dark red wine from Spain, now known mostly to crossword solvers.
explanation.definitionFit: Discontent is dissatisfaction, a lack of contentment.

clue.text: Steer over turn in river

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: to con a ship is to direct its steering
a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: Someone steers over a bend in the river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Congo flows through central Africa and is the second longest river on the continent.

clue.text: Just a minute before …

parts.note: ere is a poetic word for before

explanation.surface: Wait a moment before the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries the sentence on into the next clue; it adds nothing to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Mere means only or nothing more than, as in a mere child.

clue.text: Nasty horn here: cow, is it?

definitions.text: Nasty horn here: cow, is it?

indicators.note: nasty letters are made disagreeable, rearranged into a new form

explanation.surface: Someone sees a vicious horn and wonders if it belongs to a cow.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: an animal with a nasty horn that might be taken for a cow.
explanation.definitionFit: This large African grazing animal has a fearsome horn and could be mistaken from afar for a heavy cow.

clue.text: … Arrival seen regularly in valley

indicators.note: letters taken at regular intervals, every other one

explanation.surface: Someone arrives and is seen often in the valley.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to the previous clue for the surface only. Taking the second, fourth and sixth letters of Arrival gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A ria is a long narrow inlet formed by the sea flooding a river valley.

clue.text: Bouncer going to extremes to intervene in row

indicators.note: to come between two parts, so these letters go inside the word for row

parts.note: a tier is a row of seats

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A nightclub bouncer goes too far in stepping into a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouncer' suggests a doorman; it is the bouncy tiger in A. A. Milne's Winnie-the-Pooh. 'row' looks like a quarrel but is a tier of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiger friend of Winnie-the-Pooh is famous for bouncing on his tail.

clue.text: Poet advocating admiration of Brussels?

parts.note: love is warm admiration or affection
Brussels is famous for its handmade lace

explanation.surface: A poet speaks up for the fondness people feel for Belgium's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advocating' joins: read as a slogan, the answer urges you to love the city's famous lace. Richard Lovelace was a 17th-century English Cavalier poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Lovelace wrote To Althea, from Prison, with its line about stone walls not making a prison.
